Droplet typeface

Hat Nguyen’s family of swollen, irregular display letters for T-26, named as a signature grunge font.

Source
T.26 Digital Type Foundry: Droplet
Creator
Hat Nguyen
Made
1996 (Klingspor Museum specimen sheet)
Style
Grunge typography (partial fit; agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, organic, raw
Evidence
Inspected the Klingspor Museum specimen sheet for Hat Nguyen (a one-page PDF, rendered at about 900 × 1300) and the Fonts In Use render (779 × 176), in scratchpad copies. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Awl, quoting T-26 founder Carlos Segura, names Hat Nguyen’s Droplet among the signature grunge fonts distributed by T-26. The Awl.

The Klingspor Museum sheet lists Droplet Lite, Droplet, and Droplet Extra as 1996 T-26 releases, also sold by Linotype. Klingspor Museum.

T-26 still sells Droplet in four styles: Lite, Regular, Extra, and Closed, tagged “bloated”, “hybrid”, “ink”, and “organic”. T-26.

Observed

  • Droplet Lite is a thin, slightly wobbly sans-serif; Droplet and Droplet Extra are heavy, with swollen terminals and small, irregular counters.
  • Letter widths and stroke ends vary: the I has a hook, the Z and K are compressed, and the Extra weight’s counters close up into blobs.
  • Edges are smooth, not speckled or torn.

Why it belongs

Droplet shows that “grunge font” was also a market label for any irregular, hand-made-looking display face of the mid-1990s. For the eroded core of the style, prefer Reactor or Trixie.

Borrow

Pair one swollen, irregular display face with a clean text face for a looser, inky mood without heavy damage.
